key_insight: YSZ and intumescent thermal barrier coatings delayed fire-induced buckling and improved post-fire load retention in thin-walled cold-formed steel, with intumescent protection performing marginally better.
engineering_relevance: These coatings offer potential lightweight alternatives to bulky gypsum fire protection for cold-formed steel members.
method: Tested S355 lipped channels (150 × 50 × 2 mm) under ISO-834 fire exposure, with 10 specimens per uncoated, YSZ and intumescent group.
Tracked buckling and temperature using LVDTs and thermocouples; assessed post-fire residual strength through ASTM E8 tensile tests.
Reproduced observed behaviour using nonlinear ABAQUS models and numerically explored a functionally graded coating.
evidence_signal: Experimental comparisons across 30 specimens supported benefits from both coatings, while nonlinear finite-element models reproduced the observed behaviour.
watch_item: The functionally graded coating remains experimentally unvalidated, and implications for Eurocode 3 reduction factors require broader validation.
paper_title: Advancing cold-formed steel with thermal barrier coatings: buckling and fire resistance behaviours
